sourceAliases.note: Same source data shipping-build.js's classifyMethod already classifies for delivery-profile.json's deliveryCarrier.backupRate -- but ONLY a kind:'carrier' classification produces BOTH a DeliveryCarrier.backupRate AND a ShippingOption from the same classified method; for that kind they are not alternatives. The other kinds produce no shipping option at all: 'pickup' becomes a PickupLocation (see ecom/pickup-location), 'threshold' folds onto a sibling paid option as a conditional rate, and 'coupon-domain' produces nothing here.

preferredWrite.decision: Verified live: creating a ShippingOption that matches a region's DeliveryCarrier.backupRate populates the dashboard rate table where the carrier write alone does not.

pitfalls.summary: DeliveryCarrier.backupRate does not create a ShippingOption and does not clear Wix's missing-rates dashboard warning. Live verification showed that a carrier-only region can write and read back successfully while remaining non-functional at checkout. Always create a matching ShippingOption for every imported DeliveryRegion from the same classified method used for DeliveryCarrier.backupRate; see shipping-build.js's buildShippingOptionInput.

CORRECTED. An earlier reading of this API said to use the singular `deliveryRegionId` and treat the plural as decoration; that is inverted. Per the service contract, the singular `deliveryRegionId` is DEPRECATED and replaced by `deliveryRegionIds`, with a removal target already in the past -- the plural is the live field, which is also why the singular-only observation showed an empty plural array on read-back. Write BOTH: the plural is what is honoured going forward, the singular keeps older reads and tooling working until it is actually removed. The original observation was real; the conclusion drawn from a doc page that predated the deprecation was not.

The field is `estimateDeliveryTime`, NOT `estimatedDeliveryTime`. The wrong spelling is accepted by the create call and SILENTLY DROPPED, so a run writing it looks completely successful and leaves every option with a blank delivery estimate. Confirmed against the service contract's own field list and its shipped create example. Separately, Wix's own shipping-setup guidance treats a blank value as a defect to avoid; shipping-build.js's buildShippingOptionInput defaults it to '5-7 business days' when the caller doesn't override, since WooCommerce has no equivalent field to source a real value from.

`rates[]` is the ConditionalRates type: each entry is {conditions[0..10], amount (decimal string), multiplyByQuantity}, and each Condition is {type: BY_TOTAL_WEIGHT|BY_TOTAL_PRICE|BY_TOTAL_QUANTITY, value, operator: EQ|GT|GTE|LT|LTE}. Conditions AND together; an empty conditions[] means always-applies. The runtime rule, verbatim from the service contract: 'at runtime for a given shipment input, up to one rate (price) should be returned in an option. If more than one rate is valid then we return the lowest one.' A source minimum-order free-shipping threshold is therefore fully expressible and is NOT a gap. What the contract does NOT settle is whether BY_TOTAL_PRICE is measured before or after cart discounts -- WooCommerce has an explicit ignore_discounts setting for exactly this, so the two can disagree. Ship the threshold as written, flag it, confirm at the first live checkout, and never report such a rate as verified until then.

CORRECTED, and the correction matters more than the original. An earlier version of this rule said each carrier-classified method becomes its own ShippingOption and to never collapse several methods into one. That produces a store where the same delivery is listed two or three times, because a source zone lists every shipping BEHAVIOUR as its own method row -- a minimum-order threshold and a coupon-gated free shipping are both rows, and neither is something a buyer picks. Observed live: one source zone with five methods produced four options, two of them byte-identical unconditional zeroes. Resolve the zone's methods to buyer-facing choices first (shipping-build.js's resolveZoneMethods: fold thresholds onto paid options, drop coupon-gated rows, route pickup to its own entity, then collapse identical survivors) and create one option per surviving choice. Every collapse is reported as a resolved source defect -- a silent collapse is indistinguishable from never having noticed.

mappingGuidance: For every WooCommerce shipping-zone method that shipping-build.js's classifyMethod resolves to kind:'carrier', create BOTH a DeliveryCarrier (backupRate, on the delivery profile) AND a ShippingOption (rates[], standalone resource keyed by deliveryRegionId) from the same classified result -- shipping-build.js's buildDeliveryCarrierInput and buildShippingOptionInput. Creating only the former leaves the region looking fully configured via the API (and even via a plain Query Delivery Profiles read-back) while Wix's own checkout and dashboard still treat it as missing rates.
amount is a plain decimal string ('8', '0'), same convention as backupRate.amount -- no separate currency/format handling needed.

A source minimum-order free-shipping threshold is CARRIED, not dropped: write the paid option with two rates, an LT band at the source price and a GTE band at 0, both on BY_TOTAL_PRICE at the source's minimum. The explicit two-way split is preferred over relying on the lowest-valid-rate tiebreak, so the merchant sees the same two bands in the dashboard that the source had. shipping-build.js's priceThresholdRates builds it.

An unconditional 0-amount rate is correct in exactly one case: a source free-shipping method with NO condition attached at all. Anywhere else it means a condition was dropped, which does not half-migrate the rule -- it inverts it, makes every paid option unreachable, and costs the merchant its shipping revenue. shipping-build.js's verifyShippingEconomics fails a region that has an unconditional free option alongside a paid one, for exactly this reason.
objectPageException: The standard API reference menu (dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/e-commerce/shipping-delivery, checked 2026-08-15) has exactly one subsection, 'Delivery Profiles' -- no 'Shipping Options' subsection and no dedicated ShippingOption '…-object' page exist anywhere in that tree. The entire resource is undocumented there; the only place it's described at all is the 'Shipping: API Reference' skills article (a distilled, AI-agent-oriented reference in a completely separate doc tree, business-solutions/e-commerce/skills/) plus its sibling 'Fix Shipping Coverage Gaps' article. The full field shape is sourced from those two pages' request/response examples instead.
